surfaces.part: rock wall face with central crack

answer.evidence: The silhouette is a constant 16 px wide for rows 0-63, so there is no widening, no ellipse and no roof or lintel plane. Row 0 is only a dark 1-row outline, and the mixed grey and dark crack texture continues straight down from row 1. No row has a front-edge line followed by eave shadow, and nothing shows a horizontal surface. Rows 0-46 are a vertical cliff face with a dark crack at about x=8. Rows 47-63 are a vertical band of water mist and green foliage. The whole drawing is a flat front elevation of a wall with no top surface, not a gate, pavilion or building.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a narrow cliff or chasm face strip, not a building. It has no roof, walls, door or windows, so it does not match the reference kind. It is also far smaller than the references, about 1 tile wide. Its measured facts are 10 visible tones per tile, against 12 and 10 for the references, and 0% near-flat coverage, so the density numbers alone would not fail it. But 85% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral, against 7% and 9% for the references, which confirms the black, untinted outline of the sticker look. By eye the stone face has only about 3 grey steps with dark cracks. It lacks the per-stone shading and tinted dark material outlines of the Beodeul stone wall and tile roof, and its small green patch at the bottom is the only variation. It reads as thinner and flatter than the references.
